surface_mechanism_description: The exposure of the surface to the oxygen precursor caused an abrupt mass decrease, which is explained by the replacement of iodine, adsorbed together with titanium during the TiI4 pulse, by much lighter oxygen or hydroxyl groups in the reaction with H2O or H2O–H2O2. The shape of the mass sensor response to the H2O pulse showed that the surface reaction was relatively slow and not entirely completed when the growth temperature was reduced to 140 8C. The mass decrease, which appeared after switching off the oxygen precursor pulse, indicated that some amount of reaction products and/or precursor was removed from the surface during the purge time. The reactions proceeded somewhat faster with H2O–H2O2 than with H2O.
evidence: The exposure of the surface to the oxygen precursor caused an abrupt mass decrease ( Fig. 1). An explanation for this kind of effect is that iodine, which was adsorbed together with titanium during the TiI4 pulse, was replaced by much lighter oxygen or hydroxyl groups in the reaction with H2O or H2O–H2O2. The shape of the mass sensor response to the H2O pulse (Fig. 1a ) showed that the surface reaction was relatively slow and not entirely completed, when the growth temperature TG was reduced to 140 8C. The mass decrease, which appeared after switching off the oxygen precursor pulse, indicated that some amount of reaction products and/or precursor was removed from the surface during the purge time. The reactions proceeded somewhat faster with H2O–H2O2 (Fig. 1b) than with H2O (Fig. 1a).
